To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
i) 3D skeletal data improves SL recognition, ii) 2D skeletal and hand region representations are complementary and iii) the proposed 3D pose estimation technique is accurate and robust to occlusions.
(1) 3D hand joint coordinates are beneficial in the task of SL recognition from RGB videos; and (2) 3D human hand joint coordinates are successfully inferred from RGB videos.
3D hand joint coordinates are beneficial for SL recognition and can be reliably inferred from RGB data, even in the absence of depth data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the exploitation of 3D skeletal data in deep learning based SL recognition from RGB videos.

the following contributions: (a) a 3D hand joint estimation technique that is trained on a large dataset and achieves state of the art performance, (b) the first investigation on the benefits of 3D information to the task SL recognition, (c) an attention based encoder-decoder for the fusion of multiple streams of SL informative features, (d) a new state of the art for isolated sign and continuous finger spelling SL recognition.

the following contributions: (a) we investigate the benefit that 3D hand information can bring to the task of SL recognition, (b) we demonstrate how the 3D pose estimation technique can be applied to SL data, (c) we report state of the art results in SL recognition from RGB data and (d) we provide an open source implementation of the 3D estimation technique
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, while 3D hand information is indeed beneficial for SL recognition from RGB video, it is not a necessity and the 2D skeleton is a sufficient representation of SL in the context of the proposed recognition system.
the inclusion of 2D and 3D hand information is beneficial to the task of SL recognition, while the 3D estimates are also of high accuracy on their own.

our proposed 3D hand estimation technique, when used as a standalone, outperforms the state of the-art on the 2D hand joint estimation task on the challenging MPII dataset, but falls short of the state of the- art in the 3D joint estimation task on a smaller dataset, namely the Human3.6M dataset.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new method to estimate 3D hand poses from RGB data that is competitive with the state of theart.

3D hand information, which is not available in traditional SL datasets, can be inferred from RGB data, providing a significant boost to recognition accuracy, while also outperforms the state of the arts in 3D human body pose estimation.
the proposed 3D hand estimation technique is able to provide useful information to the SL recognition task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 3D coordinates can be successfully estimated from a single image and that this information can be used to improve SL recognition performance.
3D hand joint information can be reliably estimated from RGB data, thus providing a useful source of information for the recognition of SL from video data.

the proposed method for 3D hand joint estimation from RGB data, which is trained and evaluated on a SL corpus, outperforms the state of theart, which was originally introduced for 3D human skeleton estimation from RGB videos, and is trained and evaluated in a generic fashion, i.e. on a dataset of generic human poses.
